title: Real 3D skin layers on 1.21.11
description: On 1.21.11 the skin overlay now has genuine depth: the proper 3D Skin Layers is built in and runs on its own, so the hat, jacket, sleeves and trousers stand off the body as real geometry that follows the skin. The old approximation was removed there, and its toggle went with it since the layers are on by default. The 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds keep the built in approximation for now while the same depth is ported to them.
changes: 1.21.11 ships real 3D skin layers with genuine depth, on by default
The old skin layer approximation and its toggle are gone on 1.21.11
26.1.2 and 26.2 keep the current approximation until the port lands

title: 3D skin layers built the right way
description: The skin layers were scaled before, which stretched the sleeves and trousers off the limbs. They are now built as larger boxes that stand off the body evenly, the way it is meant to be done, so nothing stretches. The Depth slider sets how far they stand off; after changing Depth or the toggle, reload with F3+T for it to take effect.
changes: 3D skin layers stand off as evenly built boxes instead of stretched scaling
The Depth slider sets how far they stand off
Changing Depth or the toggle applies after a reload with F3+T
Same across the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Saturation is an outline around the food
description: Saturation now draws a thin outline that follows the edge of each drumstick, with nothing inside, so the food stays fully visible and the outline sits only around it. One outlined drumstick per two points of saturation. The colour is still yours from the module's settings.
changes: Saturation is a thin outline around the food, not a fill or a line
One outlined drumstick per two points of saturation
Same across the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Skin layers stop stretching the limbs
description: The 3D skin layers grew on every axis, which stretched sleeves past the hands and trousers past the feet. They now thicken to stand off the body without getting any longer than the limb they cover, so the shape stays right. The Depth slider still sets how far they stand off. A fuller, texture built version of the layers is on the way.
changes: Skin layers thicken to stand off the body without stretching the limbs longer
The Depth slider sets how far they stand off
Same across the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Thinner saturation, real skin layers, joinable friends, blur strength
description: Saturation is now a thin line that hugs the bottom of the food and grows with the saturation behind it, instead of the box that sat around it. The 3D skin layers stand off the body far enough to actually see, and the Depth slider drives how far. When the Effects module is on it takes over completely: the vanilla effect icons step aside so only BestClient's list shows. Friends can be joined straight from Discord now, and the presence carries the server so the Join button appears for them. Motion blur has five strength steps from Faint to Max instead of three.
changes: Saturation is a thin line under the food, sized to how much saturation is behind it
3D skin layers stand off the body enough to see, with the Depth slider setting how far
The Effects module hides the vanilla effect icons and shows only its own
Discord shows a Join for the server you are on, and joining from it launches you in
Motion blur has five strengths, Faint to Max
Same across the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Saturation sits at the edge of the food now
description: Saturation used to paint over the whole food. It is now a two pixel border at the edge of the food it backs, so the food stays visible and the border grows and shrinks with how much saturation is behind it. The colour is still yours from the module's settings.
changes: Saturation is a two pixel border around the saturated food, not a fill over it
The border widens and narrows with the amount of saturation
Same in the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Sign in that stays, a lean install, and tidier friends
description: Signing in used to be dropped the moment a session refresh failed, so a second offline was enough to log you out for good. Now only Microsoft actually retiring the sign in ends it; a network blip keeps you signed in. A fresh install now sets up only the essentials, BestClient with Fabric API, Sodium and Lithium, with nothing extra to switch on or off. The friends list shows the service's own wording instead of raw errors, checks more often so requests arrive sooner, and parties go up to ten. Two modules that shared an icon in the Right Shift menu now have their own.
changes: The Microsoft sign in survives network trouble and only ends when Microsoft actually retires it
A new install sets up only BestClient, Fabric API, Sodium and Lithium, with no optional mods to toggle
The friends list shows plain wording, not raw errors, and refreshes sooner
Parties go up to ten players
Motion blur and Sprint no longer share an icon with another module

title: Saturation shows on the food, the way AppleSkin does it
description: The saturation module drew a box around the food bar. It now sits on the food itself, one drumstick per point of saturation, filling from the top for a half point, which is how AppleSkin shows it. The colour is still yours to pick from the module's settings by right clicking it. The 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds match.
changes: Saturation draws a filled overlay on each food icon it backs, with a partial icon for a half point, like AppleSkin
The colour stays customisable from the Saturation module settings
Same in the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: The update finds its own download, and the code ships obfuscated
description: Checking for an update used to ask the GitHub API where the installer was, which sits on a sixty an hour limit for anyone not signed in, so a run of checks could leave the update unable to find its own file and download nothing. It now builds that address itself from the version, with no such limit. The launcher's own compiled code is also obfuscated before it ships now, so it no longer reads like source once unpacked. Nothing secret was ever kept in the client, so this changes how hard it is to read, not what it protects.
changes: The update builds the installer address itself instead of asking the rate limited GitHub API, so the download stops failing after repeated checks
The launcher's compiled code is obfuscated in the shipped build
No behaviour change to the modules or the game

title: Motion blur actually blends, and the module list has a scrollbar
description: Motion blur keeps the last frame in a buffer and mixes it into the next one, but that buffer was not marked to survive between frames, so the game was free to reuse it and the blend had nothing real to blend against. It is now a persistent buffer, so the blur builds up the way it should. The module list in the Right Shift menu also gained a scrollbar on the right, so it is clear when there is more below the fold. Both the 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds get the same.
changes: Motion blur holds its previous frame in a persistent buffer, so it blends instead of doing almost nothing
The module list has a scrollbar down the right side
Same in the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Motion blur that stays clean
description: Motion blur held onto the world it was first switched on, so leaving to the menu, rejoining a server or stepping through a portal left it off until you toggled it again. It now follows you onto each new world and keeps blending. The blend shader was also written for a newer GL version than the game asks for, which is why some drivers refused it and switched it off; it now matches the game's own post shaders, so it compiles where the game does. The same fix ships for the 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds.
changes: Motion blur reapplies itself after leaving to the menu, rejoining, or changing dimension, instead of quietly staying off
The blend shader targets the same GL version the game uses, so drivers that refused it before now run it
Same fix in the 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2 builds

title: Motion blur, a sprint module, and more to set on the crosshair
description: Motion blur is in, as a module under Visual with three strengths. It is off by default and it needs testing: it works by asking the game to run a blend of the current frame with the previous one, using the same post effect format the game's own blur and invert use, and it has never been run here. If your graphics driver refuses it, it switches itself off and says so in the log rather than leaving you with a broken screen. The sprint module makes sprint a toggle instead of something to hold, and can sprint whenever you walk forwards. The crosshair indicator gains opacity, and a switch for whether it answers to players only or to any living thing.
changes: Motion blur module, three strengths, off by default and switches itself off if the driver refuses it
Sprint module: toggle instead of hold, and an always sprint option
Crosshair indicator: opacity, and players only or any living thing
Both new modules have their own settings under Visual

title: The stutter is gone, and two lines of text with it
description: The frame rate log was writing itself to disk on the render thread, which meant the game hitched every half minute because of the thing measuring how smoothly it ran. That write now happens on a background thread, less often. The launcher was also polling the friends service every few seconds while the game was in front of it, so it now asks for nothing at all until the game closes. The ready line under the Play button and the line confirming the Discord connection are both gone.
changes: The frame rate log no longer writes on the render thread, which was a hitch every 30 seconds
The launcher stops polling entirely while the game is running
The ready line under the Play button is gone
The Discord confirmation line is gone, and only real problems are reported

title: The crosshair indicator is adjustable, and the FPS reads properly
description: The indicator has settings of its own now: size, and whether it inverts the background the way the game's crosshair does or is painted in a colour you pick. Module names in the right shift menu no longer run off the end of their tile. The FPS module has an icon that reads as a frame rate rather than a filmstrip, and the launcher shows the last session's average with its worst second and the last dozen sessions behind it, so a change is something you can see.
changes: Crosshair indicator: size, invert or colour, under its own settings
Module names are trimmed to their tile instead of overflowing it
The FPS module has a new icon
The launcher shows the average, the worst second, and a bar per recent session

title: The crosshair is the mod's, nothing else, and versions can take small steps again
description: The client's own crosshair is gone. It drew a pink cross of its own over the game's, and it was the thing that looked wrong. What is left is exactly what the mod does and nothing more: the game's own crosshair, untouched, with four small corner brackets drawn after it while you are aiming at a player. Versions can carry a fourth number again, so a small fix goes out as 0.8.9.1 rather than spending a patch number and pushing towards 0.9.
changes: The client's custom crosshair is removed, along with its settings
The game's crosshair is left exactly as it is, with the indicator drawn after it
One switch under Visual, Crosshair indicator, and nothing else to set
Versions can take a fourth number, so releases step in smaller increments

title: The crosshair indicator, rebuilt the way the mod does it
description: The previous two attempts drew the indicator from the client's HUD layer, which was the wrong place for it. The crosshair render pipeline does not paint, it inverts whatever is already on screen underneath. Drawn last, after the whole HUD, the brackets were inverting the hotbar and the health bar instead of the world, which is why it looked broken. It is now drawn from inside the crosshair render itself, the same injection point the mod uses, so the only thing behind it is the world.
changes: The indicator is drawn from inside the crosshair render, not from the HUD layer
On 1.21.11 that is the same method and the same tail injection the mod uses
On 26.2 and 26.1.2 the equivalent, which sits on a different class in each
It still appears when the client's own crosshair has replaced the game's

title: The crosshair indicator now looks right
description: 0.8.7 drew the indicator as a plain white texture, so it painted over the background instead of standing out from it and looked wrong against anything pale. The game draws its own crosshair through a pipeline that inverts what is behind it, which is how it stays readable on snow and on coal alike, and the mod this came from uses that same pipeline. Now so does the client, so the brackets are pixel for pixel what the mod draws.
changes: The indicator uses the crosshair render pipeline, so it inverts the background instead of painting over it
Checked against the mod's own compiled code: same pipeline, same draw call, same size, same position
The mod build script accepts any JDK 21 or newer instead of only 21

title: A new crosshair indicator, on all three versions
description: The indicator that appears when you are aiming at a player is now the one from the Crosshair Indicator mod: four small white corner brackets, drawn from its own artwork, instead of the larger pink brackets the client drew before. It has its own switch under Visual and works over the game's own crosshair, so it no longer needs the custom crosshair turned on. That mod is built for 1.21.x and cannot load on Minecraft 26 at all, so it is drawn by the client itself and looks the same on 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2.
changes: The player indicator is now four small corner brackets, from the Crosshair Indicator artwork
It has its own switch under Visual, separate from the custom crosshair
It draws over the game's own crosshair, so nothing else has to be turned on
The same on 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2

title: Minecraft 26 starts
description: This is why 26.1.2 and 26.2 never worked. Minecraft 26 moved its native libraries into subfolders: the game is told to look in natives/java, while every launcher release so far wrote them into natives directly. The folder the game looked in was empty, so it died before loading a single mod, with an error that named whichever mod touched graphics first. Sodium was getting the blame for a launcher bug. The natives are now placed where each version asks for them, read out of that version's own manifest rather than guessed from its number. Parties are fixed too: they broke the moment the database moved, because the new tables were created with a different collation than the ones that came across.
changes: Minecraft 26.1.2 and 26.2 start, with natives written where 26 expects them
The right architecture wins when several builds of a native library are offered
A missing native library is reported as an install problem, not as the mod that tripped over it
Parties work again after the database move
The service can no longer answer an error with a page of HTML and a stack trace

title: Play starts the game, the crash tells you what broke, and the FPS is on screen
description: Pressing Play used to walk 5121 asset files, check 155 libraries, hash every mod and ask Modrinth twice, every single time, even when nothing had changed since the last launch. All of that now happens quietly in the background while the launcher is open, so Play just starts the game. When the game does crash, the launcher reads the crash report and says which mod caused it, with a button to switch that mod off. And the frame rate the mod already measures is now kept, so the launcher can show what the last session averaged and whether that is better or worse than usual.
changes: Play starts the game straight away when nothing has changed
Everything is checked in the background, and the mods folder is watched for changes
A crash now names the mod that caused it, with one button to turn it off
Out of memory, graphics driver and native crashes are explained in plain words
The average FPS of your last session, compared against the ones before it
Party invites arrive in about three seconds instead of twenty
The online player count refreshes every twelve seconds instead of every sixty
Neither keeps polling while the launcher window is hidden

title: Parties, a setup that follows your account, and one version number
description: Friends can now be pulled into a party that holds together across restarts, with a clock counting the session and a Join button that takes you straight onto the server a friend is playing on. Your setup lives on your Minecraft account: reinstall Windows, sign in, and the memory, mods, HUD, keybinds and first ten servers come back. The heap is picked from the machine instead of a fixed default, and the version number now comes from one place, so the Windows uninstall entry stops claiming 0.5.5.
changes: Parties: invite a friend, see who is in, and follow the leader to their server
A party clock that counts from when the party formed and survives a restart
Join a friend straight from the friends list, onto the server they are on
Your setup is kept on your account and restored after a reinstall
Each part of that setup is its own switch in Settings
The first ten servers in your multiplayer list travel with the account
The memory is picked from the machine, with the slider still there if you want it
One version number across the launcher, the installer and the uninstall entry

title: A zoom you can set up, and the mod check leaves our own jar alone
description: The zoom module has the settings it was missing: hold or toggle, smooth zoom in and out, smooth camera movement, scroll to zoom with its own speed, the zoom level, and a separate sensitivity while zoomed so turning at 4x is usable. The mod check no longer sends the client's own jar to Modrinth, which it was never going to find.
changes: Zoom can be held or toggled
Smooth zoom in and out, and smooth camera movement while zoomed
Scroll to zoom, with its own speed setting
A separate mouse sensitivity that applies only while zoomed
The mod check skips the BestClient jar instead of asking Modrinth about it

title: The new mark, everywhere it belongs
description: One icon now stands for BestClient in every place Windows and Minecraft show it: the taskbar, the installer, the mods list in the launcher, and the mod menu inside the game. The launcher title bar keeps the plain mark on its own, without the tile behind it.
changes: The taskbar and installer carry the new BestClient icon
The mod menu in game shows it for BestClient, on all three Minecraft versions
The launcher mods list shows it too
The title bar keeps the plain mark, with no tile behind it

title: A live player count, a fixed friends list, and a quieter look
description: Friend avatars were broken because the service that drew them went down, so they come from somewhere else now. The friends panel was rebuilt around the part that needs an answer: requests sit in their own frame with a written out Accept button instead of two identical squares. The title bar shows how many people are in game on BestClient right now. The mods and Modrinth pages no longer let the purple wallpaper show through, the console snaps up instead of sliding, and the partner servers take less room.
changes: Friend heads load again, with a second source if the first is down
Friend requests are easier to tell apart from the list, and Accept says Accept
The title bar shows how many people are playing on BestClient
The mods and Modrinth pages sit on a solid dark panel
The console log snaps up quickly instead of sliding in
Partner servers are smaller
Settings drops the changelog and links the terms and privacy policy instead

title: The client mod runs on 26.2 and 26.1.2
description: The in-game half of BestClient only ever existed as a 1.21.11 build, and the launcher copied that same file into the 26.2 and 26.1.2 folders as well. Fabric refuses a mod built for another version, so on those two profiles the game would not start at all. The mod is now built separately for each of the three versions, and the launcher installs the one that matches the version you picked.
changes: The BestClient mod is built for 26.2 and 26.1.2, not only 1.21.11
The launcher installs the mod that matches the version you are playing
A client mod left behind for a different version is cleared out of the mods folder
The HUD, client menu, zoom, fullbright and the tab list badge all work on 26.x

title: Friends work, and the game starts fast
description: The friends sign in used the account id in the wrong format, so it was refused and the whole friends system stayed dark, including the BestClient tab list icon that depends on it. That is fixed on both ends now, so the friends list, requests, and the tab list icon all work. Startup also drops the custom class cache that could rebuild on every launch and uses the built in one instead, so the game opens quickly.
changes: The friends sign in now sends the account id in the format the service expects, so signing in works
Friend requests, accepting, removing, and online status all work
The BestClient icon shows next to players who use the client in the tab list
Startup uses the built in class cache, so the game no longer rebuilds it and starts slowly

title: The game starts quickly again
description: The class cache the game uses to start faster was tied to a fixed file name. After a Java runtime change that file no longer matched, so the JVM printed a shared archive error and rebuilt the cache on every launch, which made starting the game slow. The cache file is now named after the exact Java build, so it is written once and reused, and a stale one is cleared away.
changes: The startup class cache is keyed to the Java build, so it stops mismatching and rebuilding every launch
A stale cache from an earlier Java runtime is removed automatically
No more shared archive warning in the log at launch

title: Quicker start and a cleaner saturation ring
description: The launcher opens faster. The window appears right away, and the update check and Discord presence start a moment later so they stay out of the way of the first paint. The saturation overlay now draws a thin outline on the outside of the food instead of tracing the inside of each drumstick, and it is still switched on or off from Right Shift under Modules.
changes: The launcher window shows sooner, so starting up feels faster
The update check and Discord presence start after the window is up, not before it
Saturation is a one pixel outline around the outside of the food, not an inner lining
Saturation stays on or off from Right Shift, under Modules

title: A shorter, wider streak card
description: The streak card takes less height and more width. The running count and the best and today figures sit side by side on one row instead of stacked, the total moved up next to the title, and the card widened to 420 pixels.
changes: The streak card is shorter: the count and the two figures share a row instead of stacking
It is 420 pixels wide, so the day bars have more room
The total playtime moved up beside the Streak title

title: The streak card grows sideways
description: The card is back to the height it had before and reaches further left instead: 400 pixels wide, with the same type sizes and the same bar strip as it had. The extra width goes into the day bars, which now have room to breathe.
changes: The streak card is the height it was, and 400 pixels wide
The day bars are wider, since the card no longer grows downwards

title: The friend list knows where to call
description: The client now talks to client.bestpvp.eu for the friend list and the tab list badge. The address travels in the build, the database password never does: it stays on the server and the client only ever sees the small API in front of it.
changes: The friend list and the tab list badge point at client.bestpvp.eu
They start working the moment the service answers there, with no further update needed

title: A streak card you can actually read
description: The streak card grew from 248 to 344 pixels wide, the running count is half again as large, the day bars are taller, and it appears on narrower windows than before. The FPS module carries a film frame now, because frames per second is what it counts.
changes: The streak card is 344 pixels wide, with a larger count, larger rows and taller day bars
It shows from 1220 pixels of window width instead of 1300
The FPS module icon is a film frame

title: Friends, and the client says its own name
description: The right rail is a friend list now: ask someone by their Minecraft name, answer the requests that come in, and see who is online and which server they are on. In game, the tab list marks everyone running BestClient with the logo, and servers are told the client is BestClient instead of Fabric.
changes: A friend list on the right: add by name, accept or turn down, remove, with online state and the server each friend is on
The tab list puts the BestClient logo in front of everyone on the server who runs the client
Servers now see BestClient as the client name, not Fabric
The streak card is wider and sits beside the play button
A new FPS module icon
The changelog moved to the bottom of Settings

title: The streak sits on the play screen
description: The streak card left the top of the changelog and moved one column to the left, into the empty space beside the play button, where it has room to be read. Every line now carries its own icon.
changes: The streak card sits beside the play button instead of on top of the changelog
A flame on the streak, a cup on the best run, a clock on today and an hourglass on the total
The changelog starts at the changelog again

title: Bring a Modrinth profile straight in
description: Drop a .mrpack on the mods page, or pick one with the new button, and the whole profile comes across: every mod is pulled from Modrinth and checked against the hash in the pack, and the config, resource packs, shaders and schematics are copied into the instance. Saturation now traces the food icon exactly, one pixel around its own outline.
changes: Import .mrpack on the mods page, by button or by drag and drop, with a line telling you where it is
Mods come down from Modrinth and are checked by hash, so an imported profile passes the launch check
Jars bundled inside the pack are left out by name and reason, a hacked client hidden in one never lands in your mods folder
A pack built for another Minecraft version says so instead of quietly mixing the mods in
The imported mods carry their real names, icons and versions, so they update like anything else
Packs written with a data descriptor read correctly now, the old reader gave up on most of their files
Saturation traces the food icon itself, one pixel around its outline, half a shank included
The status effect module shows nothing at all when you carry no effects, background included
A new FPS icon

title: It says what it is doing, and a streak on the right
description: The wait after pressing Play is no longer silent: the mods folder check now reports what it is reading and how far it has got, and it reads the jars four at a time instead of one after another. The right rail carries a streak card with the days you have played.
changes: The mods folder check reports its progress instead of leaving the button looking dead
The jars are hashed four at a time, so the check finishes in a fraction of the time on a big mod folder
A streak card on the right: days running, best run, time today, total, and the last fourteen days as a bar for each
Playtime is recorded per day when the game closes and kept for a year

title: Play works again when Modrinth does not
description: Pressing Play could do nothing at all: the mods folder check runs before any progress is shown, and if Modrinth did not answer it sat there and then refused to start the game. It now says what it is doing from the first moment, and an unreachable Modrinth no longer stops the game.
changes: Play reports Checking the mods folder straight away instead of sitting silent
If Modrinth cannot be reached the game starts anyway. An outage on their side is not a reason to keep you out of yours, and the check for hacked clients runs on your own machine either way
The client mod is checked against the hash the launcher ships with, never through Modrinth
The launcher log says so on the console when it cannot write itself, instead of going quiet

title: A crosshair that tells you when you are on a player, and a faster start
description: The crosshair stays a plain cross and answers with four corner brackets the moment you are looking at a player. Saturation traces the shank itself in the client pink. The game also keeps a class cache between launches, so the second start is quicker than the first.
changes: The crosshair no longer spreads. It stays a cross, and four corner brackets appear around it while you are looking at a player
Saturation hugs the shank outline itself, pixel for pixel, in the client pink
Armor has four flat colours and nothing in between: white above three quarters, green above half, orange above a quarter, red under it
A round performance mark for FPS
The module grid scrolls
Status effects: nothing at all when you are carrying none, the name in white and the time in grey
The layout screen says BestClient under the mark, with a soft shadow behind it
The game keeps a class cache between launches, so every start after the first loads fewer classes from scratch
Networking: IPv4 first so a connect cannot stall on an IPv6 route that goes nowhere, DNS answers cached for a minute, and netty leak sampling off the packet path

title: Status effects, saturation the way AppleSkin draws it, and armor that counts down
description: A status effect module with the time left on each one. Saturation is now an outline hugging each shank, half lit for half a shank, instead of a box around it. Armor counts what is left rather than what is gone, and the skin layers stay under the armour worn over them.
changes: Status effects module: every effect you are carrying with the time left, sorted by whichever runs out first
Saturation traces the shank it covers instead of boxing it in, and a half shank gets half an outline
Armor shows the durability left again, with the colour still telling you how far gone the piece is
3D skin layers no longer push through the armour worn over them: a part wearing a piece is left flat
The keystroke block has no plate of its own any more, only the key faces
The preview in a module settings card is sized to the module, so the bottom row of keystrokes is no longer cut off
The layout screen carries the BestClient wordmark under the mark
A different icon for FPS

title: Installs that fail once no longer fail for good
description: The store gave up on a mod after four quick tries and then told you nothing but the address it had tried. It now waits when Modrinth asks it to, keeps its own calls under the rate limit, stops retrying answers that will never change, and says what actually went wrong.
changes: A 429 from Modrinth is now honoured: the launcher waits the time the header asks for instead of hammering the same address four times in two seconds
The launcher holds its own Modrinth calls under 240 a minute, so a search, an update check and an install at once cannot trip the limit
A 404 or a bad request fails at once instead of being repeated four times
Failures say what happened: rate limited, timed out, not found, or could not reach the server
Every request gets a 15 second timeout and the whole retry chain a 45 second one, so a silent host cannot hold a click for two minutes
The log panel survives a mod that floods it: past 200 lines a second the rest are counted and reported instead of being pushed through one by one

title: Grimffa joins the partner servers
description: grimffa.xyz is on the Play screen with the others: live player count, MOTD and icon, and a double click launches the game straight into it.
changes: New partner server: grimffa.xyz

title: Icons instead of labels, and armor tells you what it has cost
description: FPS, ping and memory no longer spell their own name next to the number, they carry an icon. The armor block now counts the durability spent rather than what is left, coloured by how far gone the piece is.
changes: The readouts carry an icon instead of a unit label: FPS, CPS, facing, speed, ping, time, session and memory. Coordinates keep XYZ, because no icon says which three numbers those are
Armor counts the durability spent, white while untouched, then green, orange and red as a piece nears breaking
The categories down the left of the menu carry an icon
Playtime has its own stopwatch instead of sharing the hourglass
The right-click hint across the top of the menu is gone
The settings card for a module with nothing to adjust no longer runs its line off the bottom edge

title: Fix the crash on startup
description: 0.6.0 could not start: the zoom key registered the BestClient key category a second time, and the game refuses a duplicate. Both keys share the one category now.
changes: Fixed the startup crash: Category bestclient:menu is already registered

title: Zoom, a crosshair of your own, 3D skin layers, and saturation on the food bar
description: Four new things in the Right Shift menu. Saturation moved to where you actually look for it: a ring around each shank on the food bar, so you can see the buffer you are carrying. The layout screen lost its instruction box, and the plate under every readout is now half transparent.
changes: Saturation is drawn on the food bar itself: a ring around each shank the buffer still covers, half lit for a half shank
Zoom, held on mouse button 4 by default, with the zoom level in its own settings
Crosshair module: dynamic spread that opens on the attack cooldown and while sprinting, with gap, length, thickness, centre dot and colour all adjustable
3D skin layers: the hat, jacket, sleeves and trousers stand off the body instead of lying flat on it, with the depth adjustable
The instruction box at the top of the layout screen is gone
The plate under every readout is half transparent
The BestClient row on the Mods page carries the client artwork

title: Armor durability, saturation, and a plate under every readout
description: Two new modules in the Right Shift menu: armor durability, drawn as the four pieces you are wearing with the hits each one has left, and saturation. Every readout now sits on a rounded black plate at thirty percent, so the numbers stay readable over snow, sand and a lit sky.
changes: Armor durability module: your four worn pieces with the durability left under each, counting down through gold and red as a piece wears out
Saturation module
Every readout is drawn on a rounded black plate at thirty percent opacity, on by default. It is still per module: turn the plate off for any of them in its own settings

title: The client mod shows its own mark on the Mods page
description: The BestClient row in your own mods now shows the mark whole. It was being cropped to fill the rounded tile, so the edges of the wave were cut off.
changes: The BestClient icon on the Mods page is drawn inside the tile instead of cropped to fill it

title: The mod keeps its own icon
description: The BestClient mark is used inside the client menu and the layout editor, as intended. The icon the mod itself carries in the mod list is the original one again.
changes: The mod list icon is back to the original artwork
The new mark stays where it was asked for: the client menu header and the layout editor

title: One menu for the overlay, one for the modules
description: Right Shift now opens the overlay itself: every module you have switched on, laid out on the screen, with the mark and a MODULES button in the middle. MODULES is where you switch things on and off, and a right-click on any module opens its own settings. Starting the game also stops rearranging the rest of your desktop.
changes: Right Shift opens the layout screen first: drag any module you have switched on, with the BestClient mark and a MODULES button held in the centre the whole time
MODULES opens the grid you already know; Esc walks back one screen at a time
Right-click a module for its own settings: scale, accent colour, label, text shadow, backing plate, and a shortcut straight to placing it
The centre guide lines are gone from the layout screen
The real mark is now the logo everywhere: the launcher title bar, the client menu and the mod list

Starting the game no longer minimises whatever was behind the launcher. The game opens at the size of your screen instead of switching the display mode, which is what Windows answered by rearranging every other window

title: Put the overlay where you want it
description: Every readout in the client menu now has a place on the screen as well as a switch. Right-click a module and drag it wherever you want it - one screen, every module you have switched on, the real thing at the real size. The client also stops taking the display over when it starts, and asks the machine for less memory until it needs more.
changes: HUD layout editor: right-click any module in the Right Shift menu, drag it anywhere, snap it to the edges or the centre. R puts everything back
Positions are stored as a fraction of the screen, so a layout survives fullscreen, GUI scale and another monitor
Starting the game no longer takes over the display, so whatever you had open stays where it was - borderless fullscreen is part of the client set now
The heap starts at a third of the memory slider and grows into it, and hands memory back when the game goes idle. The slider is the ceiling, not the reservation
Startup flags: concurrent GC held off the render thread, string deduplication, and LWJGL argument checks skipped in the render loop
Vanilla settings tuned further without a mod in sight: biome blending off, clouds off, entities scaled at range, chunk builds at no priority
Discord presence says what it is doing in Settings - connected and as whom, waiting for Discord, or refused and why. It also no longer loses the handshake when Discord splits it across two packets
In game: the BestClient mark sits beside the wordmark, and the white line across the top of the card is gone
The version chip and its pencil are white
New artwork for 26.1.2

title: Modrinth shows what you already have
description: Searching Modrinth used to hide every mod the client already ships, so looking one up came back empty. They are all there now, marked as installed, and Update only appears on the ones that actually have a newer build.
changes: The Modrinth search lists installed mods too, marked Installed instead of Download
Update is shown only where a newer build exists - on both the Modrinth and the Mods screen. It used to appear on rows whose build the launcher simply did not know
Updating a mod that belongs to the client updates it in place instead of installing a second copy under the store’s name, which is what put the same mod in the list twice
A build installed by an older version of the launcher is recognised again, so its old jar is removed rather than left beside the new one
The renderer list drops the line about taking effect on the next launch
The Mods screen drops the "Client" tag next to BestClient’s own mods
In game: the menu says BESTCLIENT as one word, and the "ESC to close" line is gone from the bottom corner

title: The renderer is called OpenGL
description: Sodium is OpenGL - Minecraft’s own renderer with its drawing rewritten - so the client now says OpenGL and installs Sodium behind it. The third choice, OpenGL without Sodium, was the same renderer only slower, and it is gone.
changes: The renderer chip reads OpenGL and is the default. It is the Sodium path, named for what it draws with rather than for the mod
Sodium is no longer a choice of its own, and plain OpenGL without it has been dropped - anyone on it moves to OpenGL with Sodium on the next start
Vulkan is unchanged, and still only offered on the Minecraft versions VulkanMod builds for
Where Vulkan has no build there is one renderer, so the chip states it instead of opening a list with a single line in it

title: One build of each mod, and a renderer list nothing covers
description: Updating a mod now takes the old jar out as well as putting the new one in. Two builds of the same mod in the folder is a game that closes the moment it opens, and it was possible to end up there by pressing Update all.
changes: Update all deletes the build it replaced. The folder is read jar by jar afterwards, so an older copy goes even when it was installed by hand or by an older version of the launcher
A copy you switched off yourself is left alone if it is newer than what is loading
The mods screen names every jar it deleted instead of letting one disappear quietly
The renderer list is drawn on the page itself now, so the launch button and the panels under it can no longer cover it. It still opens downward and follows the chip when the screen scrolls

title: The renderer list floats above everything it covers
description: The Sodium/Vulkan/OpenGL dropdown now stacks above the panels and readouts underneath it while it is open - before, elements further down the page could paint over its items. It still opens downward.
changes: The renderer picker dropdown is lifted in z-order so its items always paint above the content below them
Still opens downward from the picker button

title: Settings: cleanup in one place, update check on demand
description: Clear cache and Clear logs share a single Storage section in Settings, and a new Check update section forces a refresh whenever you want - when a build is downloaded the top bar offers the install.
changes: Clear cache and Clear logs merged into one Storage section in Settings
New Check update section: forces an update check and shows what the launcher found
Version bumped to 0.5.6.1

title: version.json now tells the truth
description: The update check compared against a hidden build number, which forced version.json on GitHub to carry a version nobody saw. It compares against the release number now, so the file matches the release.
changes: The launcher compares updates against the release number it shows (0.5.4.x), not the internal package version
version.json on GitHub now carries the same number as the release - no more stray 0.5.5

title: MOTD emojis in the game's own alphabet, and a zoom that actually zooms
description: The version picker's cards ease into their zoom now, and every symbol in a partner server's MOTD - and name and player count - is drawn in a true pixel alphabet, the same cut the game uses.
changes: Version picker: the artwork smoothly zooms in on hover, eased over a second instead of jumping
Partner servers: the bundled font is now the full pixel alphabet the game is built on (GNU Unifont), so skulls, hearts, swords, bombs, flowers and the rest of it come out blocky like in the game
More emojis are rewritten to their classic game symbol before drawing, and colour-emoji variation selectors are stripped first

title: The renderer menu opens downward, and the client shows its own version
description: The Sodium/Vulkan picker on the Play screen drops its menu below the button again, and the About panel shows the release number itself instead of a son-of-a-different-name.
changes: The renderer picker menu opens downward, under the button
The launcher's About panel now shows the release version (0.5.4.2) it was shipped under

title: Renderer mods are mandatory, and the picker opens upward
description: Whichever renderer you pick on the Play screen, its mod is now a required part of the pack: Sodium when the renderer is Sodium, VulkanMod when it is Vulkan, always resolved to the newest build that fits the version. The renderer menu also opens above its button now, the only four mods that are on by default are BestClient, Sodium, Fabric API and Lithium - and they are on, not off. The resource pack and shader switch is gone from Settings, and the Memory text reads again.
changes: Sodium is mandatory while the renderer is Sodium, VulkanMod while it is Vulkan - locked in the pack, resolved to the latest build at install time
The Sodium/Vulkan menu on the Play screen opens above its button instead of below
By default the client installs BestClient, Sodium, Fabric API and Lithium and nothing else - all four enabled
Removed the "Resource packs and shader" switch from Settings; the launcher no longer offers any look to install
Fixed the broken text in the Memory section - the garbled characters are proper again

title: Pick your renderer, and a client that starts empty
description: The renderer is now a choice on the Play screen - Sodium, Vulkan or plain OpenGL - and each one installs the mods that belong to it. A fresh client arrives with four mods and no resource pack, because what you add should be what you asked for.
changes: Renderer picker beside the version: Sodium, Vulkan (VulkanMod) or Minecraft’s own OpenGL. Each installs its own set, and Vulkan is only offered where it has a build
The client now starts with Fabric API, Sodium, Lithium and BestClient, and nothing else - everything else is one switch away on the Mods screen
Resource packs and the shader are off by default and have their own switch in Settings
Fabric API can no longer be turned off: the BestClient mod depends on it
In-game: "Hurt camera" is now "No hurt cam" and works the way the rest of the menu does - switching it on removes the tilt. It read backwards before, so turning it on appeared to do nothing
In-game: the brightness slider is gone; fullbright stays
Partner servers: names, player counts and MOTDs are all in Minecraft’s own alphabet
New artwork for 26.2, and the version cards ease into their zoom instead of snapping to it

title: The launcher checks the mods against each other before the game does
description: Two mods that refuse to load together used to reach you as "exited with code 1". The launcher now reads what every jar demands of the others, settles the disagreement by holding one mod a build back, and says plainly what happened when it cannot.
changes: Every installed jar is read before launch and checked against the others, including the libraries bundled inside them and inside Fabric Loader itself
A mod that cannot load beside another is stepped back through its own older builds until one fits - Sodium Extra now yields to the Sodium build Nvidium needs, instead of stopping the game
When nothing fits, the Play screen names both mods and both versions instead of leaving you a number
A crash now shows what the game actually said, not only its exit code
The launcher log is written straight to disk, so its last lines survive a crash
Sound Culling is offered only on 26.1.2 and 26.2, the versions it is published for
Update all: white text

title: The launcher checks the mods against each other before the game does
description: Two mods that refuse to load together used to reach you as "exited with code 1". The launcher now reads what every jar demands of the others, settles the disagreement by holding one mod a build back, and says plainly what happened when it cannot.
changes: Every installed jar is read before launch and checked against the others, including the libraries bundled inside them and inside Fabric Loader itself
A mod that cannot load beside another is stepped back through its own older builds until one fits - Sodium Extra now yields to the Sodium build Nvidium needs, instead of stopping the game
When nothing fits, the Play screen names both mods and both versions instead of leaving you a number
A crash now shows what the game actually said, not only its exit code
The launcher log is written straight to disk, so its last lines survive a crash
Sound Culling is offered only on 26.1.2 and 26.2, the versions it is published for
Update all: white text

title: The in-game menu is real, and six mods for a smoother game
description: Right Shift now opens the client menu it was always meant to open - its own look, its own typeface, thirteen modules - and fullbright finally works. Six mods join the pack, including one that stops fullscreen from throwing Discord out of fullscreen.
changes: The BestClient mod is built and shipped for the first time: Right Shift opens a menu with its own artwork, typeface and thirteen modules
Fullbright works - it was never actually wired up before
New modules: FPS, CPS, coordinates, direction, speed, ping, clock, playtime, memory and a WASD keystroke overlay
Borderless Fullscreen: the game no longer takes over the display, so Discord and anything else stay where they were
Sodium Extra, AsyncParticles, Smart Particles, Better Block Entities and Sound Culling join the pack
Mods screen: Update all replaces the active-mod counter
Settings: the Discord switch is labelled Discord RPC, and the startup flags box only asks for your own additions

title: Locked startup flags and a newer Java
description: The tuned startup flags can no longer be rewritten - you add to them instead - and every version now runs on the current long-term Java release.
changes: Startup flags: the tuned set is fixed and shown in full; your own flags go in their own box and run after it, so anything you add still wins
Every version runs on Java 25 now, never below what the game itself asks for
"Reset PvP defaults" is now "Reset defaults"
Update all matches the other buttons: white text on the standard grey

title: Update every mod at once
description: One button on the Mods screen moves everything to its newest build, and works out which ones cannot go together before it touches anything.
changes: New Update all button on the Mods screen
Before anything is installed, each new build's own compatibility rules are read: a build that will not work alongside another mod you have is left where it is, and named
Both directions are checked - a new build that rejects an installed mod, and an installed mod that rejects the new build
The client refuses to start if its own mod is missing or fails its hash check, instead of launching without it

title: The version sits in its own panel
description: The version and renderer above Launch now sit together in a small frosted panel, with the edit mark lined up against the version.
changes: The version and OpenGL are in their own rounded panel above the Launch button
The edit mark is centred against the version instead of sitting on its baseline

title: A bigger line above Launch
description: The version and renderer above the Launch button are larger, and the edit mark is a quiet grey that turns white under the cursor.
changes: The version and OpenGL above Launch are noticeably larger
The edit mark is grey at rest and white when you hover it
It no longer grows under the cursor - a target that moves is harder to hit

title: The version leads the line
description: Above Launch the version now comes first, with the edit mark against it, and the renderer sits behind it.
changes: The version and the label swapped places: the version leads, OpenGL follows
Only the version is clickable now - the renderer beside it is a fact, not a button
The edit mark is white and larger, and grows under the cursor

title: A roomier version picker
description: The version picker is much larger, and picking one leaves it open so you can look at the others.
changes: The picker fills far more of the window, with bigger artwork and a bigger version number on each
Choosing a version no longer closes the picker - the card lights up and you stay where you are
The "In use" tag is gone; the lit card is the answer

title: Pick a Minecraft version
description: Fight and Survival are gone. There is one mod pack - the PvP one - and you choose which Minecraft to run it on: 26.2, 26.1.2 or 1.21.11.
changes: Click the version above Launch to choose between 26.2, 26.1.2 and 1.21.11
The same mods, resource packs, shader and settings on every version
Each version keeps its own worlds and screenshots; switching never touches the others
Your installation stays where it is, on 1.21.11
Mods with no build for the version you picked are named and skipped rather than blocking the launch
Game folders left behind by an old version are cleaned up on every start - worlds and screenshots are never removed

title: Two builds: Fight and Survival
description: The client is two clients now. Fight is the PvP build it has always been. Survival is a full world on Minecraft 26.1.2 with 141 mods and 59 resource packs, and you switch between them from the line above Launch.
changes: Pick your build from the line above Launch - it has an edit mark now, and opens a card for each one
Fight: Minecraft 1.21.11, the PvP mod set and packs, exactly as before
Survival: Minecraft 26.1.2, 141 mods, 59 resource packs and 8 shaders
Each build keeps its own mods, worlds, settings and screenshots - switching never touches the other one
Your existing installation becomes the Fight build, with everything where you left it
The Java version now comes from Minecraft's own manifest, so a build that needs a newer Java gets one
Fight's mods and packs are also in Survival, sitting under Survival's own; anything with no 26.1.2 build is listed but switched off

title: The PvP pack set, and Launch signs you in
description: The client now installs its own resource packs and shader and turns them on for you, and the big button signs you in when you are signed out instead of just saying so.
changes: Five PvP resource packs install themselves and are switched on in the right order: Classic Glint, Low Fire, Low Shield, Short Swords and Teeny Totem Pop
Complementary Reimagined is installed and selected as the shader, left switched off so it costs you nothing until you want it
Everything is pinned to an exact version and checked against its hash, so a pack cannot change under you between launches
New mod: G1axNameHistory, name history and UUIDs in chat
Default settings retuned: full field of view, render distance 8, hold to sprint, no view bob, no entity shadows
Signed out, the Launch button signs you in - the code to enter appears in the account panel

title: Discord presence and four ways in, closed
description: BestClient now shows on your Discord profile, and the launcher shuts the routes a cheat client uses to get into the game behind the mod check.
changes: Discord: your profile shows whether you are in the launcher or in game, which server you joined and how long you have played, with a switch in Settings that clears it the moment you turn it off
The JVM attach mechanism is closed, which is how an injector loads itself into a game that is already running
Startup flags that can load code - Java agents, boot class path, Fabric and Mixin loader properties - are refused, in the settings box and again at launch
The launch stops if another launcher has been pointed at the game folder, because starting from it would skip the mod check entirely
The application refuses to start if its own files were edited, and can no longer be re-run as plain Node to load an outside script

title: News pictures lose the dashed outline
description: The dashed white border added in the last build is gone. Hovering a news item still turns the cursor into a pointer and lifts the picture a little.
changes: News: the dashed white outline on hover was removed
The pointer cursor and the slight lift on hover stay

title: News pictures mark themselves
description: A news item you can open now says so: the cursor becomes a pointer and the picture picks up a dashed white outline while you are over it.
changes: News: hovering an item that opens a link turns the cursor into a pointer and outlines the picture with a dashed white border
The outline takes no space when it appears, so the picture never shifts under the cursor

title: Editable startup flags, calmer news hover
description: Settings now shows the complete JVM command line the game starts with and lets you edit all of it, and news pictures answer the cursor with a much smaller lift.
changes: Settings: a new Startup flags section listing every JVM flag the launcher uses, fully editable, with the heap line shown above it and a one-click restore to the defaults
Your edits are written when you leave the field instead of on every keystroke
News: the picture lifts far less on hover

title: Single deletion notice, news pictures grow on hover
description: Clearing the cache or the logs now confirms it exactly where you clicked instead of repeating the message in three sections, and news pictures truly become bigger when you hover instead of zooming into their crop.
changes: The cache and log deletion toasts are scoped to their own section - one place, once
News: on hover the whole picture grows larger, anchored upward; the crop inside the frame no longer magnifies

title: Remembered launch behaviour, glowing launch button, softer news hover
description: The launch behaviour is a real remembered choice again (Stay open is still the default), the BestClient mod shows the same switch as every other mod - pinned on and unflippable -, news pictures light up by growing on hover instead of darkening, and the launch button glows and grows a touch under the cursor.
changes: Launch behaviour: Stay open, Minimise launcher and Hide launcher are all back as a real choice, defaulting to Stay open; the launcher remembers what you picked even after a full close
BestClient mod: the same switch as every other mod, sitting in the on position - it just cannot be flipped, from the UI or from the main process
News: on hover the picture now grows a little inside its box; the card no longer darkens
Launch game button: a soft brand glow and a slight grow under the cursor

title: BestClient mod always on, stay-open launcher, static two-column news
description: The bundled mod is installed at startup and is always on with no way to switch it, the launcher only ever stays open after launching the game, the news section is a static two-column grid with bigger, never-zooming pictures, the GPU line is gone, and the RAM icon is bigger and grey.
changes: BestClient mod: installed as soon as the launcher starts and always on - the Mods list shows a fixed On pill instead of a switch, and the main process refuses to touch it
Launch behaviour: Stay open is the only option now, set as the default for everyone; the launcher remembers it from launch to launch
News: a static two-column grid at fixed 16:9 banners, pictures bigger; no zoom on hover, more items just continue below on the page scroll
The GPU model line was removed from the Play screen and Settings - no more telling you what video card you have
RAM icon: bigger and grey instead of the small rose chip

title: Fixed 16:9 window, Minecraft-font MOTDs, bundled in-game mod
description: The launcher is a fixed 1366x768 canvas now, partner-server MOTDs are drawn with Minecraft's own pixel font, the in-game BestClient mod ships inside the installer, and Settings gained dedicated, iconed Cache and Logs sections.
changes: The window is a fixed 1366x768 16:9 canvas - slightly bigger than before, not resizable and not maximizable, so every screen is built exactly for that size
Partner-server MOTDs render in Minecraft's own pixel font, bundled with the client: skulls, swords, hearts and stars look like in-game text instead of colourful Windows emojis
News: the grid is a static three columns and every banner lives in a fixed 16:9 box; hovering grows the picture inside its box without moving anything around it
Settings: Clear cache and Clear logs moved out of Maintenance into their own sections, each with its own icon
Update checks run twice as often (every 15 minutes) and the news/changelog feeds refresh every minute instead of every five
The BestClient mod is now bundled in the installer (SHA-1-stamped against tampering): Right Shift opens the in-game menu in Minecraft, starting with Fullbright
Closing the launcher while the game is running no longer disturbs it - the game keeps running on its own

title: BestClient mod, store, news and changelog feed, GPU detection fix
description: The client ships with its own in-game mod (fullbright, no hurt camera, a Right Shift menu), the launcher grows a store, a market, news and changelog rails, and the NVIDIA default is now decided from every adapter instead of just the first one.
changes: In-game mod: Fullbright toggle and brightness slider, hurt camera toggle and a client menu on Right Shift, settings saved in bestclient.json
Store and market views with the full catalog, so the client's own content has a home
News feed and changelog rail on the home screen, pulled straight from GitHub
Self-updater: version.json in the repo is the single source the launcher polls; downloads and verifies the installer by SHA-256
GPU detection: every adapter is checked now, so a hybrid laptop reports NVIDIA even when Chromium lists the integrated card first; an unknown GPU is never persisted as a wrong default
Maintenance actions in Settings to clear caches and logs
Server ping and inventory details on the game page, bundled mods stamped at install time
Release admin: version.json, changelog.json and news.json drive the whole flow

title: NVIDIA optimization switch, instant mod updates, GPU-aware defaults
description: A new Settings switch tailored to the detected GPU adds Nvidium and Reflex to the modpack on NVIDIA cards, and the Mods list can update any mod to its newest build in one click.
changes: Settings: NVIDIA optimization switch - adds Nvidium and Reflex Anti-Lag to the modpack; on by default on NVIDIA GPUs, off on AMD and Intel, decided from your actual hardware on first run; turning it off removes the mods again
Mods list: an Update chip appears left of the version button when a newer build exists, and clicking it swaps in the newest version instantly
News banners grow only when the cursor is on the picture itself, and the faint hairline on the left edge is gone
The delete button just tints red on hover instead of going solid red
The RAM slider knob is plain rose - no black ring, no shadow

title: Injection protection, borderless Launch button, chip RAM readout
description: The launcher checks the mods folder for known hacked clients and injectors before every launch, the Launch Game button lost its border, and the RAM readout shows a memory chip instead of "max".
changes: Before every launch the mods folder is checked against known hacked clients and injectors such as Doomsday, LiquidBounce and Aristois - by file name, and by scanning the bytes of Modrinth-approved jars, so a renamed injector cannot sneak in; anything flagged blocks the launch with its own warning
Launch Game has no border - just the clean rounded brand-coloured button
The RAM readout shows a memory-chip icon instead of "MAX"
Store sort menu items have a small gap between them
News banners zoom less on hover; "Double-click to join" is properly capitalised

title: Richer store cards, custom sort dropdown, opaque panels
description: Store cards now show the author, category tags and download/follower counts, the sort control is a custom rounded dropdown, and the popup panels are solid instead of translucent.
changes: Store cards show the author, up to three category tags, and download and follower counts with a heart
The store's result order is a custom rounded dropdown that matches the rest of the UI
Mods list: the version button is right-aligned and always shows the full version string
News banners alternate left and right in the two-column layout, and growing on hover no longer shifts the text below
Partner-server cards and the account-switcher popup have solid, opaque backgrounds

title: Bigger news banners, Stay-open default, build dropdown
description: News banners are larger and grow on hover instead of zooming, the launcher stays open by default when the game starts, and switching a mod's build is a dropdown next to the version button.
changes: News banners are bigger; on hover they grow instead of zooming, so the picture's edges are never clipped
Settings: new "Stay open" option, on by default - the launcher keeps its window when the game starts; Minimise launcher and Hide launcher remain
The build picker is now a dropdown attached to the version button, opening above or below it depending on the space
The on/off switches use a darker, stronger green

title: White button text, restored button colours, clean news banners
description: The buttons say their text in white over the familiar colours again, the build-picker popup works exactly as before, and the news banners are back to natural size without a dark backing box.
changes: Button text is white; button backgrounds are the 0.2.0 look (brand-pink Download and Browse files, grey Search, pager, Update)
The build-picker popup and its buttons work as in 0.2.0
News banners: no black backing box, natural size, bigger gap between items
Partner-server MOTDs rewrite Windows colour emojis to Minecraft-font symbols
Store, mod list and Settings keep the soft rounded panel behind the content

title: Minecraft-style MOTDs, white buttons and softer panels
description: Partner-server MOTDs speak in Minecraft's own symbols instead of Windows colour emojis, the store, the mod list and the settings sit on a rounded panel in front of the wallpaper, and every solid button is white now.
changes: Partner-server MOTDs: Windows colour emojis are rewritten to Minecraft's monochrome symbols
Modrinth, the mod list and Settings sit on one soft rounded panel, inset from the edges of the page
Solid buttons - Search, Download, Update, Browse files, pager, settings - are white instead of dark
News moved further down, banners shown at natural size without cropping or stretching
Hovering a news item zooms its banner slightly
The memory slider has a thicker, brand-pink knob

title: Partner servers, the changelog rail and in-game BestClient
description: The Play screen now shows live partner-server status you can join with a double-click, the mod list finally covers everything that is actually installed, and the client ships with its own in-game mod.
changes: Partner servers: live player count, MOTD and server icon, queried directly from the server
Double-click a partner server to launch straight onto it
Fixed the server lookup so a server published on an SRV record is reachable
New changelog rail down the right-hand side, on every screen
The mod list now shows pack mods, Modrinth installs and jars you added yourself, all in one place
Search your own mods, and switch any mod to a different Modrinth build
Modrinth store: sorting, twelve results per page, and a grid that never leaves a half-empty row
BestClient's own mod ships with the client and cannot be removed - Right Shift opens the in-game menu
The game console rises from the bottom the moment a launch starts
Automatic update check, with the install left to you
Hardened the launcher: strict content policy, allow-list sanitizer for remote content, and stricter file handling

title: First build
description: Microsoft sign-in, the Fabric 1.21.11 install pipeline, the Modrinth store and the PvP-tuned defaults.
changes: Microsoft device-code sign-in with multiple accounts
Fabric 1.21.11 install pipeline with automatic dependency resolution
Modrinth store for extra mods
PvP-tuned JVM flags and options.txt baseline
